title: Steve Jobs: April Fools to One Device
description: A garage startup, an ouster, and one pocket that ate three gadgets—Go Deep into April Fools to one device.

questions.question: Jobs, Wozniak, and a third founder who sold his 10% for $800 two weeks later started Apple on April Fools' Day of what year?
questions.explanation: Ronald Wayne drew the first Apple logo, then got spooked by the partnership's debts. That $800 slice would later be worth tens of billions.

questions.question: The 1976 startup's first mass-produced hit, the machine that put a color computer on desks in 1977, was called what?
questions.explanation: Mostly Wozniak's design. VisiCalc, the first spreadsheet, turned it from a hobbyist toy into a business machine.

questions.question: After the Apple II era—and after the board pushed him out—Jobs founded what computer company Apple later bought back?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee built the first web server and browser on a NeXT cube at CERN. Apple paid about $429 million for the company—and for its OS.

questions.question: NeXT's OS became the foundation under macOS and iOS. In January 2007 Jobs teased "an iPod, a phone, and an internet communicator"—then revealed what one device?
questions.explanation: Prototypes were so secret that employees worked on locked-down floors. The audience gasped when the three gadgets on slide one collapsed into one.

questions.question: Even after the iPhone, most of Jobs's fortune came not from Apple but from what animation studio he bought from George Lucas in 1986?
questions.explanation: Disney bought Pixar for $7.4 billion in stock in 2006, making Jobs its largest individual shareholder overnight—and putting him back on Disney's board.

imageHint: 🍎 Think different - from garage startup to tech empire 📱

deeperMode.title: The Perfectionist's Obsessions
deeperMode.description: Perfectionism and controversy behind the brand

questions.question: Jobs was famous for his demanding perfectionism. What did he reportedly make his team redesign 67 times for the first iPhone?
questions.hint: The container that holds the product - he wanted the 'unboxing experience' to be perfect

questions.question: What Zen Buddhist practice did Jobs follow that influenced Apple's minimalist design philosophy?
questions.hint: A practice of mental focus and awareness that values simplicity and presence

easterEgg.title: The first web server
easterEgg.text: Tim Berners-Lee built the World Wide Web's first server and browser on a NeXT cube at CERN. When Apple bought NeXT, that same OS lineage became the heart of macOS and iOS.
